name: Sunoh.ai vs Freed
title: Sunoh.ai vs Freed: Affordable AI Medical Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Sunoh.ai and Freed AI scribes for clinicians. See differences in pricing, multilingual support, EHR integration, and features.

summary.bottom_line: Both are affordable AI scribes for solo and small practices. Sunoh.ai ($149/mo) offers multilingual support and eClinicalWorks partnership; Freed ($39-119/mo) has tiered pricing, free trial, and more EHR push integrations. Choose Sunoh for multilingual practices or eClinicalWorks users; choose Freed for lower starting price and broader flexibility.

sections.heading: Sunoh.ai vs Freed: Overview
sections.content: Sunoh.ai and Freed are both affordable AI medical scribes aimed at solo practitioners and small practices, making them direct competitors. Sunoh.ai has achieved significant scale with 100,000+ providers and is known for multilingual support and a strategic eClinicalWorks partnership. Freed has 10,000+ clinicians with tiered pricing starting lower ($39/mo) and broader EHR push integrations on Premier. Both offer ambient listening, mobile apps, and EHR integrations. The choice often comes down to language needs, EHR preference, and pricing flexibility.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Freed offers more pricing flexibility with three tiers: Starter ($39/mo, 40 notes), Core ($79/mo, unlimited), and Premier ($119/mo, EHR push + ICD-10). Sunoh.ai has a flat $149/provider/month for unlimited visits. For light users, Freed is cheaper; for high-volume providers, Sunoh's flat rate may be simpler. Freed offers a 7-day free trial without credit card; Sunoh's trial availability is less clear. Both are significantly more affordable than enterprise solutions like Dragon Copilot.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Sunoh.ai's key differentiators are multilingual support for diverse patient populations and a strategic eClinicalWorks partnership offering deep integration for eCW users. Freed's advantages are tiered pricing flexibility, more native EHR push integrations (Athenahealth, SimplePractice, Elation, Tebra on Premier), ICD-10 coding suggestions, and a free trial. Both have mobile apps and ambient listening. For mental health practices, Freed explicitly supports therapy note formats; Sunoh focuses more on primary care.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your language needs and EHR:

recommendations.when: You serve multilingual patient populations, use eClinicalWorks (strategic partnership), prefer flat-rate pricing, or are a high-volume primary care practice
You want to try before buying (7-day free trial), prefer tiered pricing for lower entry cost, need ICD-10 coding suggestions, or want native push to SimplePractice or Athenahealth
You're a mental health professional—Freed explicitly supports psychiatry and therapy note formats while Sunoh focuses more on primary care

faqs.q: Which is cheaper: Sunoh.ai or Freed?
faqs.a: It depends on usage. Freed starts at $39/month (40 notes) vs. Sunoh's $149/month flat. For unlimited notes, Freed Core is $79 and Premier is $119, both cheaper than Sunoh's $149. Sunoh's value is simplicity with one price for everything.

faqs.q: Does Freed support multiple languages like Sunoh?
faqs.a: Freed advertises 90+ language transcription. Sunoh is specifically known for multilingual support as a key differentiator. Both can handle diverse patient populations, though Sunoh has made it more central to their positioning.

faqs.q: Which is better for eClinicalWorks users?
faqs.a: Sunoh.ai has a strategic partnership with eClinicalWorks offering deeper integration. Freed works with eClinicalWorks via browser extension. For eCW users wanting the tightest integration, Sunoh is the better choice.

faqs.q: Does either work for mental health documentation?
faqs.a: Freed explicitly supports mental health with psychiatry notes and therapy progress notes as listed note types. Sunoh focuses more on primary care, internal medicine, and family medicine. For mental health practices, Freed is likely the better fit.
